FULL STATUTORY TEXT — ENROLLED VERSION

    Enrolled Copy                                                                          H.B. 21

1                  Criminal Code Recodification and Cross References

                                   2025 GENERAL SESSION

                                   STATE OF UTAH

                              Chief Sponsor: Matthew H. Gwynn

                                   Senate Sponsor: Keith Grover

2
3 LONG TITLE

4 General Description:

5   This bill modifies criminal provisions in Title 76, Utah Criminal Code, by redrafting

6 offense statutes into a new structure, reorganizing criminal statutes into a new format, and

7 clarifying existing law.

8 Highlighted Provisions:

9   This bill:

10  ▸ reorders language into a standardized format and clarifies existing law, including the

11 offenses in Title 76, Chapter 9, Offenses Against Public Order and Decency, and

12 Chapter 10, Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, Welfare, and Morals;

13  ▸ reorganizes Title 76, Chapters 9 and 10 into a new organization to better align with the

14 contents of the statutes;

15  ▸ reorganizes offenses to enact an embedded offense as a stand-alone statute or statutes,

16 including offenses concerning:

17  ● emergency reporting, interference, and false reports;

18  ● prohibited use of a party line or public pay telephone;

19  ● commercial obstruction;

20  ● electronic communication harassment and disclosure of personal information;

21  ● cruelty to animals, dog fighting, and police service canines, including aligning

22 exemptions and defenses based on the elements of each offense;

23  ● voyeurism;

24  ● abuse or desecration of a dead human body;

25  ● criminal street gang activities;

26  ● tobacco sales and related offenses;

27  ● gambling and related offenses;

28  ● bus hijacking and related offenses;
    H.B. 21                                                                         Enrolled Copy

29           ● money laundering and related offenses;

30           ● the use of a laser pointer;

31           ● unlawful littering and related offenses;

32           ● unlawful possession, use, or control of a vehicle with a contraband compartment;

33           ● unlawful tattooing or piercing of a minor;

34           ● labeling of explosives and related offenses;

35           ● weapons offenses and related statutes;

36           ● corporate fraud and related offenses, including unlawful acts by a director, officer, or

37 agent;

38           ● nuisances;

39           ● pornography and related offenses, including placing the definition of pornography in

40 the relevant definition section;

41           ● prostitution, sexual solicitation, and related offenses; and

42           ● kickbacks and related offenses;

43  ▸ for clarity, places contents of Title 76, Chapter 9, Part 5, Libel, into Title 45, Chapter 2,

44 Libel;

45  ▸ for clarity, places certain contents of Title 76, Chapter 10, Part 5, Weapons, into Title 53,

46 Public Safety Code;

47  ▸ for clarity, places certain law enforcement requirements concerning gang loitering from

48 Title 76, Chapter 10, Part 9, Prohibition of Gang Activity, into Title 53, Chapter 25, Law

49 Enforcement Requirements;

50  ▸ for clarity, defines a minor as an individual younger than 21 years old for the offense

51 concerning public intoxication;

52  ▸ for clarity, provides a more detailed description of an actor for purposes of offenses

53 involving providing a weapon to a minor;

54  ▸ for clarity, technically revises language concerning vicious animal offense;

55  ▸ for clarity, removes definition of image in offense concerning failure to report child

56 sexual abuse material by a computer technician;

57  ▸ adds penalty provisions to offenses concerning high explosives that had been

58 inadvertently omitted;

59  ▸ repeals certain statutes concerning the Utah Trade Commission, which entity no longer

60 exists;

61  ▸ for clarity, provides which prostitution-related offenses do not apply to a minor;

62  ▸ makes technical corrections to certain statutes resulting from inadvertent omissions in the

                                                - 2 -
    Enrolled Copy                                                                           H.B. 21

63 2024 criminal code recodification, including:

64  ● reinserting a provision guaranteeing Native American rights in the statute concerning

65 establishment of a prohibited item policy in a correctional or mental health facility;

66  ● reinserting the penalty to the offense of alteration of proposed legislative bill or

67 resolution; and

68  ● providing clarifying language regarding the identity of the actor in the offense

69 concerning trafficking in warrants; and

70  ▸ makes technical and conforming changes.

71 Money Appropriated in this Bill:

72  None

73 Other Special Clauses:

74  None

911  Section 1. Section 4-2-903 is amended to read:

912  4-2-903 . Animal care violations.

                                        - 27 -
     H.B. 21                                                                               Enrolled Copy

913 (1) "Animal care facility" means the same as that term is defined in Section [76-9-301.9]

914  76-13-215.

915 (2) The department may, in accordance with this section and as resources allow, respond to

916  a complaint that an animal care facility has violated Subsection [76-9-301(2)(a)]

917  76-13-202(2)(a) or Section [76-9-301.9] 76-13-215.

918 (3) If the department determines that a person has violated Subsection [76-9-301(2)(a)]

919  76-13-202(2)(a) or Section [76-9-301.9] 76-13-215, the department may:

920  (a) impose a civil fine of up to $500 per violation;

921  (b) seek a temporary restraining order;

922  (c) seek an injunction;

923  (d) seek an order of seizure or condemnation for an animal that is the subject of the

924           violation, if the department has identified a suitable animal care facility that accepts

925           custody of the animal; or

926  (e) report the circumstances to law enforcement or a prosecutor.

927 (4) An action by the department under Subsection (3) may precede and does not preclude a

928  criminal penalty or criminal prosecution under Section [76-9-301 or 76-9-301.9]

929  76-13-202, 76-13-203, 76-13-204, or 76-13-215.

930 (5) The department shall deposit a fine imposed under Subsection (3) into the General Fund

931  as a dedicated credit to be used by the department for enforcement of this section.

932           Section 2. Section 4-25-303 is amended to read:

933           4-25-303 . Feral swine detrimental to state's interests -- Seizure, capture, or

934 destruction of feral swine.

935 (1) Feral swine are detrimental to the state's interests in agriculture and wildlife.

936 (2) Feral swine may be seized, captured, or destroyed at any time, in any place, and in any

937  manner by:

938  (a) the department and the department's authorized agents;

939  (b) the Division of Wildlife Resources and the Division of Wildlife Resources'

940           authorized agents; or

941  (c) a certified peace officer.

942 (3)(a) Notwithstanding [Section 76-9-301] Section 76-13-202, 76-13-203, or 76-13-204,

943  and subject to the requirements of this section, an individual may kill a feral swine

944  roaming on private or public land.

945  (b) An individual shall obtain the consent of the landowner before killing a feral swine

946           on private land.

                                              - 28 -
     Enrolled Copy                                                                                H.B. 21

947  (c) Feral swine may be killed:

948  (i) year-round;

949  (ii) in any number; and

950  (iii) with a firearm, bow and arrow, or crossbow.

951 (4) Feral swine may not be hunted or killed under Subsection (3)(c):

952  (a) with the use of artificial light or night vision equipment, except as authorized by

953  county ordinance; or

954  (b) from or with any airborne vehicle or device, except as provided in Section 4-23-106.

955 (5) An individual may not receive compensation, or attempt to receive compensation, from

956  hunting feral swine.

957 (6) An authorized individual who kills a swine under this section is not liable to the owner

958  for the loss of the swine, unless:

959  (a) the swine is conspicuously identified by an ear tag or other form of visual

960  identification; and

961  (b) the individual who killed the swine knew the swine was identified by an ear tag or

962  other form of usual identification.

963  Section 3. Section 4-41a-102 is amended to read:

964  4-41a-102 . Definitions.

965  As used in this chapter:

966 (1) "Adulterant" means any poisonous or deleterious substance in a quantity that may be

967  injurious to health, including:

968  (a) pesticides;

969  (b) heavy metals;

970  (c) solvents;

971  (d) microbial life;

972  (e) artificially derived cannabinoid;

973  (f) toxins; or

974  (g) foreign matter.

975 (2) "Advertise" or "advertising" means information provided by a person in any medium:

976  (a) to the public; and

977  (b) that is not age restricted to an individual who is at least 21 years old.

978 (3) "Advisory board" means the Medical Cannabis Policy Advisory Board created in

979  Section 26B-1-435.

980 (4)(a) "Anticompetitive business practice" means any practice that reduces the amount

                                            - 29 -
      H.B. 21                                                                     Enrolled Copy

981   of competition in the medical cannabis market that would be considered an attempt to

982   monopolize, as defined in Section [76-10-3103] 76-16-501.

983   (b) "Anticompetitive business practice" may include:

984            (i) agreements that may be considered unreasonable when competitors interact to the

985            extent that they are:

986            (A) no longer acting independently; or

987            (B) when collaborating are able to wield market power together;

988            (ii) monopolizing or attempting to monopolize trade by:

989            (A) acting to maintain or acquire a dominant position in the market; or

990            (B) preventing new entry into the market; or

991            (iii) other conduct outlined in rule.

992 (5)(a) "Artificially derived cannabinoid" means a chemical substance that is created by a

993   chemical reaction that changes the molecular structure of any chemical substance

994   derived from the cannabis plant.

995   (b) "Artificially derived cannabinoid" does not include:

996            (i) a naturally occurring chemical substance that is separated from the cannabis plant

997            by a chemical or mechanical extraction process; or

998            (ii) a cannabinoid that is produced by decarboxylation from a naturally occurring

999            cannabinoid acid without the use of a chemical catalyst.

1000 (6) "Cannabis Research Review Board" means the Cannabis Research Review Board

1001  created in Section 26B-1-420.

1002 (7) "Cannabis" means the same as that term is defined in Section 26B-4-201.

1003 (8) "Cannabis concentrate" means:

1004  (a) the product of any chemical or physical process applied to naturally occurring

1005           biomass that concentrates or isolates the cannabinoids contained in the biomass; and

1006  (b) any amount of a natural cannabinoid or artificially derived cannabinoid in an

1007           artificially derived cannabinoid's purified state.

1008 (9) "Cannabis cultivation byproduct" means any portion of a cannabis plant that is not

1009  intended to be sold as a cannabis plant product.

1010 (10) "Cannabis cultivation facility" means a person that:

1011  (a) possesses cannabis;

1012  (b) grows or intends to grow cannabis; and

1013  (c) sells or intends to sell cannabis to a cannabis cultivation facility, a cannabis

1014           processing facility, or a medical cannabis research licensee.

1020  a form that is recognizable as a portion of a cannabis plant.

2533  Section 27. Section 23A-13-303 is amended to read:

2534  23A-13-303 . Nuisances.

2535 (1)(a) A county shall exclude the activities described in Subsection (1)(b) from the

2536  definition of public nuisance in a county law or ordinance regulating a public

2537  nuisance.

2538  (b) An activity or occurrence normally associated with a migratory bird production area

2539  is not a nuisance, including:

2540  (i) hunting;

2541  (ii) discharging a firearm;

2542  (iii) improving habitat;

2543  (iv) trapping;

2544  (v) eradicating weeds;

                                          - 75 -
      H.B. 21                                                                             Enrolled Copy

2545           (vi) discing;

2546           (vii) planting;

2547           (viii) impounding water;

2548           (ix) raising a bird or other domestic animal;

2549           (x) grazing;

2550           (xi) an activity conducted in the normal course of an agricultural operation as defined

2551           in Section 4-44-102; and

2552           (xii) an odor.

2553 (2) In a civil action for nuisance or a criminal action for public nuisance under Section [

2554  76-10-803] 76-9-1301, it is a complete defense if the action is:

2555  (a) normally associated with a migratory bird production area;

2556  (b) conducted within a migratory bird production area; and

2557  (c) not in violation of federal or state law.

2558 (3) An owner of a new development located in whole or in part within 1,000 feet of a

2559  migratory bird production area shall provide the following notice on a plat filed with the

2560  county recorder:

2561                                     "Migratory Bird Production Area

2562           This property is located in the vicinity of an established migratory bird production area

2563  in which hunting and activities related to the management and operation of land for the benefit

2564  of migratory birds have been afforded the highest priority use status. It can be anticipated that

2565  these uses and activities may now or in the future be conducted on land within the migratory

2566  bird production area. The use and enjoyment of this property is expressly conditioned on

2567  acceptance of any annoyance or inconvenience that may result from activities normally

2568  associated with a migratory bird production area."

5291           person.

5293  barreled rifle, or a device that could be used as a dangerous weapon from which is

5294  expelled a projectile by action of an explosive.

5295  (b) "Firearm" does not include an antique firearm.

5303  (b) "Short barreled shotgun" includes a dangerous weapon made from a shotgun by

5304  alteration, modification, or otherwise, if the weapon as modified has an overall length

5611           day on which the individual was added to the restricted list, unless the individual:

5612           (A) requests to be removed from the restricted list after 30 days;

5613           (B) requests to remain on the restricted list; or

5614           (C) directs the individual's health care provider to request that the individual

5615           remain on the restricted list;

5616           (iii) a request for an extension shall be made in the same manner as the original

5617           request; and

5618           (iv) the individual may continue to request, or direct the individual's health care

5619           provider to continue to request, extensions every 180 days.

5620  (b) For an individual added to a restricted list under Subsection (2)(b), the individual:

5621           (i) may not request removal from the restricted list unless the individual has been on

5622           the restricted list for at least 90 days; and

5623           (ii) shall remain on the restricted list, unless the bureau receives a request from the

5624           individual to have the individual's name removed from the restricted list.

5625 (7) If an individual restricted under this section is a concealed firearm permit holder, the

5626  individual's permit shall be:

5627  (a) suspended upon entry on the restricted list; and

5628  (b) reinstated upon removal from the restricted list, unless:

5629           (i) the permit has been revoked, been suspended for a reason other than under this

5630           section, or has expired; or

5631           (ii) the individual has become a restricted person under Section [76-10-503] 76-11-302.

5757           Section 84. Section 53-5d-102 is amended to read:

5758           53-5d-102 . Definitions.

5759  As used in this chapter:

5760 (1) "Ammunition" means a bullet, a cartridge case, primer, propellant powder, or other

5761  ammunition designed for use in any firearm, either as an individual component part or in

5762  a completely assembled cartridge.

5763 (2) "Manufacturer" means, with respect to a qualified product, a person who is engaged in

5764  the business of manufacturing a qualified product and who is licensed to engage in

5765  business as a manufacturer under 18 U.S.C. Chapter 44.

5766 (3) "Negligent entrustment" means the supplying of a qualified product by a seller for use

5767  by another person when the seller knows, or reasonably should know, the person to

5768  whom the product is supplied is likely to, and does, use the product in a manner

5769  involving unreasonable risk of physical injury to the person or others.

5770 (4) "Person" means the same as that term is defined in Section 68-3-12.5.

5771 (5)(a) "Qualified civil liability action" means a civil action or proceeding or an

5772  administrative proceeding brought by any person against a manufacturer or seller of a

5773  qualified product, or a trade association, for damages, punitive damages, injunctive or

                                         - 170 -
      Enrolled Copy                                                                                 H.B. 21

5774  declaratory relief, abatement, restitution, fines, or penalties, or other relief, resulting

5775  from the criminal or unlawful misuse of a qualified product by the person or a third

5776  party.

5777  (b) "Qualified civil liability action" does not include:

5778  (i) an action brought against a transferor convicted under 18 U.S.C. Sec. 924(h) or

5779          Section [76-10-503] 76-11-302 by a party directly harmed by the conduct of which

5780          the transferee was convicted;

5781  (ii) an action brought against a seller for negligent entrustment or negligence per se;

5782  (iii) an action in which a manufacturer or seller of a qualified product knowingly

5783          violated a state or federal statute applicable to the sale or marketing of the

5784          product, and the violation was a proximate cause of the harm for which relief is

5785          sought, including:

5786          (A) any incident in which the manufacturer or seller knowingly made any false

5787                 entry in, or failed to make appropriate entry in, any record required to be kept

5788                 under federal or state law with respect to the qualified product, or aided,

5789                 abetted, or conspired with any person in making any false or fictitious oral or

5790                 written statement with respect to any fact material to the lawfulness of the sale

5791                 or other disposition of a qualified product; or

5792          (B) any case in which the manufacturer or seller aided, abetted, or conspired with

5793                 any other person to sell or otherwise dispose of a qualified product, knowing,

5794                 or having reasonable cause to believe, that the actual buyer of the qualified

5795                 product was prohibited from possessing or receiving a firearm or ammunition

5796                 under 18 U.S.C. Sec. 922(g) or (n) or Section [76-10-503] 76-11-302;

5797  (iv) an action for breach of contract or warranty in connection with the purchase of

5798          the product;

5799  (v) an action for death, physical injuries, or property damage resulting directly from a

5800          defect in design or manufacture of the product, when used as intended or in a

5801          reasonably foreseeable manner, except that where the discharge of the product

5802          was caused by a volitional act that constituted a criminal offense, then the act shall

5803          be considered the sole proximate cause of any resulting death, personal injuries, or

5804          property damage; or

5805  (vi) an action or proceeding commenced to enforce the provisions of 18 U.S.C.

5806          Chapter 44, 26 U.S.C. Chapter 53, or [Title 76, Chapter 10, Part 5, Weapons] Title

5807          76, Chapter 11, Weapons.

                                             - 171 -
      H.B. 21                                                                      Enrolled Copy

5808 (6) "Qualified product" means a firearm or antique firearm, as defined in Section [76-10-501]

5809  76-11-101, ammunition, or a component part of a firearm or ammunition.

5810 (7) "Seller" means, with respect to a qualified product, a federal firearms licensee, as

5811  defined in Section [76-10-501] 53-5a-301.

5812 (8) "Trade association" means:

5813  (a) any corporation, unincorporated association, federation, business league, or

5814           professional or business organization not organized or operated for profit and no part

5815           of the net earnings of which inures to the benefit of any private shareholder or

6061 for Victims of Crime.

6063  Part 4, Sexual Offenses, ]may request a test for the HIV infection.

6070  result is not positive, follow-up testing shall occur at three months and six months after

6071  the alleged occurrence of the sexual offense.

6073  victim provides a substantiated claim of the sexual offense, does not test HIV positive at

6074  the base-line testing phase, and complies with eligibility criteria established by the Utah

6075  Office for Victims of Crime.

6828           53G-6-204 . School-age children exempt from school attendance.

6829 (1)(a) A local school board or charter school governing board may excuse a school-age

6830  child from attendance for any of the following reasons:

6831           (i) a school-age child over 16 years old may receive a partial release from school to

6832           enter employment, or attend a trade school, if the school-age child has completed

6833           grade 8; or

6834           (ii) on an annual basis, a school-age child may receive a full release from attending a

6835           public, regularly established private, or part-time school or class if:

6836           (A) the school-age child has already completed the work required for graduation

6837              from high school;

6838           (B) the school-age child is in a physical or mental condition, certified by a

6839              competent physician or physician assistant if required by the local school board

6840              or charter school governing board, which renders attendance inexpedient and

6841              impracticable;

6842           (C) proper influences and adequate opportunities for education are provided in

6843              connection with the school-age child's employment; or

6844           (D) the district superintendent or charter school governing board has determined

6845              that a school-age child over 16 years old is unable to profit from attendance at

6846              school because of inability or a continuing negative attitude toward school

6847              regulations and discipline.

6848  (b) A school-age child receiving a partial release from school under Subsection (1)(a)(i)

6849           is required to attend:

6850           (i) school part time as prescribed by the local school board or charter school

7655           substances in any of those locations; or

7657           prescription or written order for a controlled substance.

7664           before the date of the offense upon which the current conviction is based is guilty

7673           prior offense was committed within seven years before the date of the offense

7674           upon which the current conviction is based.

7675           (ii) Upon a fourth or subsequent conviction the person is guilty of a third degree

7677           the offense upon which the current conviction is based.

9625  (a) takes into account:

9626           (i) the nature and circumstances of the offense of which the defendant was found

9627           guilty; and

9628           (ii) the history and character of the defendant;

9629  (b) gives any victim present at the sentencing and the prosecuting attorney an

9630           opportunity to be heard; and

9631  (c) concludes that the degree of offense established by statute would be unduly harsh to

9632           record as a conviction on the record for the defendant.

9633 (3) Upon a motion from the prosecuting attorney or the defendant, the court may enter a

9634  judgment of conviction for a lower degree of offense than established by statute:

9635  (a) after the defendant is successfully discharged from probation or parole for the

9636           conviction; and

9637  (b) if the court finds that entering a judgment of conviction for a lower degree of offense

9638           is in the interest of justice in accordance with Subsection (7).

9639 (4) Upon a motion from the prosecuting attorney or the defendant, the court may enter a

9640  judgment of conviction for a lower degree of offense than established by statute if:

9641  (a) the defendant's probation or parole for the conviction did not result in a successful

9642           discharge but the defendant is successfully discharged from probation or parole for a

9643           subsequent conviction of an offense;

9644  (b)(i) at least five years have passed after the day on which the defendant is sentenced

9645           for the subsequent conviction; or

9646           (ii) at least three years have passed after the day on which the defendant is sentenced

9647           for the subsequent conviction and the prosecuting attorney consents to the

9648           reduction;

9649  (c) the defendant is not convicted of a serious offense during the time period described

9650           in Subsection (4)(b);

                                                  - 284 -
      Enrolled Copy                                                                              H.B. 21

9651  (d) there are no criminal proceedings pending against the defendant;

9652  (e) the defendant is not on probation, on parole, or currently incarcerated for any other

9653  offense;

9654  (f) if the offense for which the reduction is sought is a violent felony, the prosecuting

9655  attorney consents to the reduction; and

9656  (g) the court finds that entering a judgment of conviction for a lower degree of offense is

9657  in the interest of justice in accordance with Subsection (7).

9658 (5) Upon a motion from the prosecuting attorney or the defendant, the court may enter a

9659  judgment of conviction for a lower degree of offense than established by statute if:

9660  (a) the defendant's probation or parole for the conviction did not result in a successful

9661  discharge but the defendant is successfully discharged from a rehabilitation program;

9662  (b) at least three years have passed after the day on which the defendant is successfully

9663  discharged from the rehabilitation program;

9664  (c) the defendant is not convicted of a serious offense during the time period described

9665  in Subsection (5)(b);

9666  (d) there are no criminal proceedings pending against the defendant;

9667  (e) the defendant is not on probation, on parole, or currently incarcerated for any other

9668  offense;

9669  (f) if the offense for which the reduction is sought is a violent felony, the prosecuting

9670  attorney consents to the reduction; and

9671  (g) the court finds that entering a judgment of conviction for a lower degree of offense is

9672  in the interest of justice in accordance with Subsection (7).

9673 (6) Upon a motion from the prosecuting attorney or the defendant, the court may enter a

9674  judgment of conviction for a lower degree of offense than established by statute if:

9675  (a) at least five years have passed after the day on which the defendant's probation or

9676  parole for the conviction did not result in a successful discharge;

9677  (b) the defendant is not convicted of a serious offense during the time period described

9678  in Subsection (6)(a);

9679  (c) there are no criminal proceedings pending against the defendant;

9680  (d) the defendant is not on probation, on parole, or currently incarcerated for any other

9681  offense;

9682  (e) if the offense for which the reduction is sought is a violent felony, the prosecuting

9683  attorney consents to the reduction; and

9684  (f) the court finds that entering a judgment of conviction for a lower degree of offense is

                             - 285 -
      H.B. 21                                                                             Enrolled Copy

9685           in the interest of justice in accordance with Subsection (7).

9686 (7) In determining whether entering a judgment of a conviction for a lower degree of

9687  offense is in the interest of justice under Subsection (3), (4), (5), or (6):

9688  (a) the court shall consider:

9689           (i) the nature, circumstances, and severity of the offense for which a reduction is

9690           sought;

9691           (ii) the physical, emotional, or other harm that the defendant caused any victim of the

9692           offense for which the reduction is sought; and

9693           (iii) any input from a victim of the offense; and

9694  (b) the court may consider:

9695           (i) any special characteristics or circumstances of the defendant, including the

9696           defendant's criminogenic risks and needs;

9697           (ii) the defendant's criminal history;

9698           (iii) the defendant's employment and community service history;

9699           (iv) whether the defendant participated in a rehabilitative program and successfully

9700           completed the program;

9701           (v) any effect that a reduction would have on the defendant's ability to obtain or

9702           reapply for a professional license from the Department of Commerce;

9703           (vi) whether the level of the offense has been reduced by law after the defendant's

9704           conviction;

9705           (vii) any potential impact that the reduction would have on public safety; or

9706           (viii) any other circumstances that are reasonably related to the defendant or the

9707           offense for which the reduction is sought.

9708 (8)(a) A court may only enter a judgment of conviction for a lower degree of offense

9709  under Subsection (3), (4), (5), or (6) after:

9710           (i) notice is provided to the other party;

9711           (ii) reasonable efforts have been made by the prosecuting attorney to provide notice

9712           to any victims; and

9713           (iii) a hearing is held if a hearing is requested by either party.

9714  (b) A prosecuting attorney is entitled to a hearing on a motion seeking to reduce a

9715           judgment of conviction for a lower degree of offense under Subsection (3), (4), (5),

9716           or (6).

9717  (c) In a motion under Subsection (3), (4), (5), or (6) and at a requested hearing on the

9718           motion, the moving party has the burden to provide evidence sufficient to

                                       - 286 -
      Enrolled Copy                                                                               H.B. 21

9719  demonstrate that the requirements under Subsection (3), (4), (5), or (6) are met.

9720  (d) If a defendant files a motion under this section, the prosecuting attorney shall

9721  respond to the motion within 35 days after the day on which the motion is filed with

9722  the court.

9723 (9) A court has jurisdiction to consider and enter a judgment of conviction for a lower

9724  degree of offense under Subsection (3), (4), (5), or (6) regardless of whether the

9725  defendant is committed to jail as a condition of probation or is sentenced to prison.

9726 (10)(a) An offense may be reduced only one degree under this section, unless the

9727  prosecuting attorney specifically agrees in writing or on the court record that the

9728  offense may be reduced two degrees.

9729  (b) An offense may not be reduced under this section by more than two degrees.

9730 (11) This section does not preclude an individual from obtaining or being granted an

9731  expungement of the individual's record in accordance with Title 44, Chapter 40A,

9732  Expungement of Criminal Records.

9733 (12) The court may not enter a judgment for a conviction for a lower degree of offense

9734  under this section if:

9735  (a) the reduction is specifically precluded by law; or

9736  (b) any unpaid balance remains on court-ordered restitution for the offense for which the

9737  reduction is sought.

9738 (13) When the court enters a judgment for a lower degree of offense under this section, the

9739  actual title of the offense for which the reduction is made may not be altered.

9740 (14)(a) An individual may not obtain a reduction under this section of a conviction that

9741  requires the individual to register as a sex offender, kidnap offender, or child abuse

9742  offender until the registration requirements under Title 77, Chapter 41, Sex, Kidnap,

9743  and Child Abuse Offender Registry, have expired.

9744  (b) An individual required to register as a sex offender, kidnap offender, or child abuse

9745  offender for the individual's lifetime under Subsection 77-41-105(3)(c) may not be

9746  granted a reduction of the conviction for the offense or offenses that require the

9747  individual to register as a sex offender, kidnap offender, or child abuse offender.

13016  (2) An actor commits causing a catastrophe if the actor causes widespread injury or damage
13017       to persons or property by:
13018       (a) use of a weapon of mass destruction as defined in Section [76-10-401] 76-15-301; or
13019       (b) explosion, fire, flood, avalanche, collapse of a building, or other harmful or
13020
13021            destructive force or substance that is not a weapon of mass destruction.
13022  (3) A violation of Subsection (2) is:
13023
13024       (a) a first degree felony if the actor causes the catastrophe knowingly and by the use of a
13025            weapon of mass destruction;
13026
13027       (b) a second degree felony if the actor causes the catastrophe knowingly and by a means
13028            other than a weapon of mass destruction; and
13029
13030       (c) a class A misdemeanor if the actor causes the catastrophe recklessly.
13031  (4) In addition to any other penalty authorized by law, a court shall order an actor convicted
13032
13033       of any violation of this section to reimburse any federal, state, or local unit of
13034       government, or any private business, organization, individual, or entity for all expenses
13035       incurred in responding to the violation, unless the court states on the record the reasons
13036       why the reimbursement would be inappropriate.

14155  (2) An actor commits aggravated commercial obstruction if the actor:
14156       (a) enters or remains unlawfully on the premises or in a building of any business;
14157       (b) intends to interfere with the employees, customers, personnel, or operations of the
14158            business; and
14159       (c) intends to:
14160            (i) obtain unauthorized control over any merchandise, property, records, data, or
14161
14162                 proprietary information of the business;
14163            (ii) alter, eradicate, or remove any merchandise, records, data, or proprietary
14164
14165                 information of the business;
14166            (iii) damage, deface, or destroy any property on the premises of the business;
14167            (iv) commit an assault on any person; or
14168            (v) commit any other felony.
14169  (3) A violation of Subsection (2) is a second degree felony.
       (4) This section does not apply to:
            (a) an action protected by the National Labor Relations Act, 29 U.S.C. Sec. 151 et seq.,
                 or the Federal Railway Labor Act, 45 U.S.C. Sec. 151 et seq; or

18753  (2) Except as provided in Subsection (4), an actor commits aggravated cruelty to an animal
18754       if the actor:
18755       (a) tortures an animal;
            (b) administers, or causes to be administered, poison or a poisonous substance to an
                 animal; or
            (c) kills an animal or causes an animal to be killed without having a legal privilege to do
                 so.

       (3) A violation of Subsection (2) is:

18770       (d) performed by an actor who humanely destroys an animal found suffering past
18771            recovery for any useful purpose; or
18772       (e) performed by an actor who humanely destroys an apparently abandoned animal
18773            found on the actor's property.
18774  (6) For purposes of Subsection (5)(d), before destroying the suffering animal, an actor who
18775       is not the owner of the animal shall obtain:

18781            actor's own observation, if the actor is in a location or circumstance where the actor is
18782            unable to contact another individual.

18787            pay the costs of the evaluation and counseling;
18788       (b) require the actor to forfeit any rights the actor has to the animal subjected to a

22486       expunged record, may not knowingly or intentionally divulge any information
22487       contained in the expunged record to any person, or another agency, without a court
22488       order unless:
22489            (i) specifically authorized by Subsection (4) or Section 77-40a-404; or
22490            (ii) subject to Subsection (1)(b), the information in an expunged record is being
22491
                      shared with another agency through a records management system that both
                      agencies use for the purpose of record management.
            (b) An agency with a records management system may not disclose any information in
                 an expunged record to another agency or person, or allow another agency or person

                                                            - 662 -
       Enrolled Copy  H.B. 21

22492            access to an expunged record, if that agency or person does not use the records
22493            management system for the purpose of record management.
22494  (2) The following entities or agencies may receive information contained in expunged
22495       records upon specific request:
22496       (a) the Board of Pardons and Parole;
22497       (b) Peace Officer Standards and Training;
22498       (c) federal authorities if required by federal law;
22499       (d) the State Board of Education;
22500       (e) the Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice, for purposes of investigating
22501            applicants for judicial office; and
22502       (f) a research institution or an agency engaged in research regarding the criminal justice
22503            system if:
22504            (i) the research institution or agency provides a legitimate research purpose for
22505
22506                 gathering information from the expunged records;
22507            (ii) the research institution or agency enters into a data sharing agreement with the
22508
22509                 court or agency with custody of the expunged records that protects the
22510                 confidentiality of any identifying information in the expunged records;
22511            (iii) any research using expunged records does not include any individual's name or
22512                 identifying information in any product of that research; and
22513            (iv) any product resulting from research using expunged records includes a disclosure
22514                 that expunged records were used for research purposes.
22515  (3) Except as otherwise provided by this section or by court order, a person, an agency, or
22516       an entity authorized by this section to view expunged records may not reveal or release
22517       any information obtained from the expunged records to anyone outside the specific
22518       request, including distribution on a public website.
22519  (4) A prosecuting attorney may communicate with another prosecuting attorney, or another
22520       prosecutorial agency, regarding information in an expunged record that includes a
22521       conviction, or a charge dismissed as a result of a successful completion of a plea in
22522       abeyance agreement, for:
22523       (a) stalking as described in Section 76-5-106.5;
22524       (b) a domestic violence offense as defined in Section 77-36-1;
22525       (c) an offense that would require the individual to register as a sex offender, kidnap
                 offender, or child abuse offender as defined in Section 77-41-102; or
            (d) a weapons offense under [Title 76, Chapter 10, Part 5, Weapons] Title 76, Chapter

                                                            - 663 -
       H.B. 21  Enrolled Copy

22526            11, Weapons.
22527  (5) Except as provided in Subsection (7), a prosecuting attorney may not use an expunged
22528
22529       record for the purpose of a sentencing enhancement or as a basis for charging an
22530       individual with an offense that requires a prior conviction.
22531  (6) The bureau may also use the information in the bureau's index as provided in Section
22532       53-5-704.
22533  (7) If an individual is charged with a felony, or an offense eligible for enhancement based
22534       on a prior conviction, after obtaining an order of expungement, the prosecuting attorney
22535       may petition the court in which the individual is charged to open the expunged records
22536       upon a showing of good cause.
22537  (8)(a) For judicial sentencing, a court may order any records expunged under this
22538       chapter or Section 77-27-5.1 to be opened and admitted into evidence.
22539       (b) The records are confidential and are available for inspection only by the court,
22540
22541            parties, counsel for the parties, and any other person who is authorized by the court to
22542            inspect them.
22543       (c) At the end of the action or proceeding, the court shall order the records expunged
22544            again.
22545       (d) Any person authorized by this Subsection (8) to view expunged records may not
22546            reveal or release any information obtained from the expunged records to anyone
22547            outside the court.
22548  (9) Records released under this chapter are classified as protected under Section 63G-2-305
22549       and are accessible only as provided under Title 63G, Chapter 2, Part 2, Access to
22550       Records, and Subsection 53-10-108(2)(k) for records held by the bureau.

25694         Section 538. Section 81-9-204 is amended to read:
25695         81-9-204 . Custody and parent-time of a minor child -- Custody factors --
25696
25697  Preferences.
       (1) In a proceeding between parents in which the custody and parent-time of a minor child

            is at issue, the court shall consider the best interests of the minor child in determining
            any form of custody and parent-time.
       (2) The court shall determine whether an order for custody or parent-time is in the best
            interests of the minor child by a preponderance of the evidence.
       (3) In determining any form of custody and parent-time under Subsection (1), the court
            shall consider:
            (a) for each parent, and in accordance with Section 81-9-104, evidence of domestic

25702            (ii) material harmful to minors, as "material" and "harmful to minors" are defined in
25703
25704                 Section [76-10-1201] 76-5c-101; and
25705       (c) whether custody and parent-time would endanger the minor child's health or physical
25706
